standard_prerequisites.name: The valuative criterion of separatedness and separatedness via tensor products
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Schemes, Lemma schemes-lemma-separated-implies-valuative (tag 090L); Varieties, Lemma lemma-glue-separated (tag 09MW)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first excludes a valuation ring dominating two of the local rings and the second converts that into surjectivity of A_i tensor A_j -> K.

standard_prerequisites.name: Glueing local rings along a field and the affine containment criterion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Varieties, Lemmas lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings (tag 09N1) and lemma-points-in-affine (tag 09NJ)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first builds the semi-local ring A with Spec(A_i) as an open covering and the second converts the resulting morphism into an affine open containing the points.

core_obligations: Set A_i equal to the local ring of X at x_i and show that no valuation ring of the function field K can dominate both A_i and A_j: the displayed square together with the valuative criterion of separatedness would force x_i = x_j (proof lines 9025-9039).

Deduce from the glueing criterion that A_i tensor A_j -> K is surjective for i not equal to j, and conclude that A = A_1 cap ... cap A_r is a Noetherian semi-local ring with exactly r maximal ideals whose localizations are the A_i, with Spec(A) covered by the Spec(A_i) with pairwise intersections Spec(K) (proof lines 9039-9051).
Glue the morphisms Spec(A_i) -> X into a morphism Spec(A) -> X that maps the maximal ideal m_i to x_i and induces isomorphisms on local rings (proof lines 9051-9056).
Apply the affine containment criterion for points with isomorphisms of local rings to conclude that the prescribed points lie in an affine open (proof lines 9057).
proof_roadmap: Separate the points by the valuative criterion so that the local rings cannot share a dominating valuation ring.
Intersect the local rings to obtain a semi-local ring with the A_i as localizations.
Glue the local models into one morphism from an affine scheme.
Apply the criterion identifying such morphisms with inclusions of affine opens.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces an affine open subscheme of an integral separated scheme X containing a prescribed finite set of points whose local rings are Noetherian of dimension at most one. The proof is a genuine construction: it shows that no valuation ring of the function field can dominate two of the local rings A_i and A_j, by the valuative criterion of separatedness applied to a square, and consequently each A_i tensor A_j -> K is surjective; it then takes A = intersection of the A_i, uses a glueing lemma to see that A is Noetherian semi-local with the A_i as its localizations at maximal ideals, verifies that the Spec(A_i) form an open covering of Spec(A) with pairwise intersections Spec(K), and glues the given morphisms Spec(A_i) -> X into a morphism Spec(A) -> X mapping the maximal ideals to the prescribed points with isomorphisms on local rings (proof lines 9025-9057). H3: the valuation-theoretic separation step and the glueing of the local models into one affine piece are independent research-level arguments.
